usize.target_fact: A TARGET fact, not an assumption: the recorded producer is trustc on aarch64-apple-darwin (a 64-bit target, the same one tests/fixtures/node_id_index.lineage.json pins), where core::mem::size_of::<usize>() is 8. On a 32-bit target the emitted body would be a different function and this table would be WRONG — which is exactly why the width lives here, in a reviewed pin, rather than as a constant inside a reader. Reader A resolved this chain with --usize-bits 64 and recorded {"usize_bits": 64, "usize_sites_resolved": 1} in its provenance; reader B resolves through THIS row and project() refuses a body whose usize site count is not exactly `sites`.
usize.erasure_note: What the resolution ERASES, said out loud: the resolved core spells the site as the plain (uint 64), so a body differing from this one only by writing `u64` where this one writes `usize` projects to the SAME core module. That swap is caught by the `sites` count above (the u64 spelling drops the observed count to 0), not by the core text — and a body with EQUAL counts but swapped positions between a usize and a real u64 would not be, which no chained body exhibits today.
